scripts.title: Head injury
steps: Make sure help is on the way. Call 911 if no one has.
Have them stop what they were doing and rest.
Ask them to keep their head and neck still.
Watch them closely for any change.
Get emergency help right away if they pass out even briefly or vomit more than once.
Do the same if they act differently, or blood or clear fluid comes from the nose, ears or mouth.
scripts.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation, and Education Guidelines 2020 (Red Cross Red Crescent)

scripts.title: Unconscious
steps: Make sure help is on the way. Call 911 if no one has.
Shout and tap them gently. Do they respond?
Check their breathing for up to 10 seconds.
If they breathe normally and no neck or back injury is suspected, roll them onto their side and tilt their head back.
If they are not breathing normally, push hard and fast in the middle of the chest.
Keep pushing until help takes over or they start breathing normally.
scripts.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation, and Education Guidelines 2020 (Red Cross Red Crescent)

scripts.title: Heavy bleeding
steps: Make sure help is on the way. Call 911 if no one has.
Put a clean cloth or clothing over the wound.
Press directly on the wound with your hands.
If blood soaks through, put another cloth on top of the first and press harder.
Keep pressing until help takes over.
scripts.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation, and Education Guidelines 2020 (Red Cross Red Crescent)

scripts.title: Fall, can't move
steps: Make sure help is on the way. Call 911 if no one has.
Don't move them.
Keep their head and neck still.
Watch their breathing until help arrives.
scripts.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation, and Education Guidelines 2020 (Red Cross Red Crescent)

scripts.title: General
steps: Make sure help is on the way. Call 911 if no one has.
Stay calm. Check that they are breathing normally.
Don't move them unless you have to.
Stay with them until help arrives.
scripts.source: IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation, and Education Guidelines 2020 (Red Cross Red Crescent)
